nodes.label: AgentFlow
nodes.description: MCP Chain-of-Thought server — a task management system with memory capability for AI programming assistants, providing structured task decomposition, execution tracking, and integrity verification. Originally named 'mcp-chain-of-thought', evolved into 'AgentFlow'.

nodes.label: Dual-Flow Architecture
nodes.description: Two execution paths: Fast Flow (no roadmap required, for simple tasks) and Structured Flow (roadmap required, for complex/ambiguous/high-risk features). Fast Flow: plan_idea → analyze_idea → review_idea → sync_tasks → execute/verify/complete. Structured Flow: same but inserts generate_roadmap before sync_tasks, then requires a Proceed/Reject decision gate.

nodes.label: Fast Flow
nodes.description: Execution path for straightforward requests (e.g., 'build a header'). No roadmap required. Steps: plan_idea → analyze_idea → review_idea (light) → sync_tasks → execute_task → verify_task → complete_task.

nodes.label: Structured Flow
nodes.description: Execution path for complex features, ambiguity, or high risk. Includes generate_roadmap step followed by a Proceed/Reject decision gate. Steps: plan_idea → analyze_idea → review_idea (iterative) → generate_roadmap → [Proceed | Reject]. If Proceed → sync_tasks → execute/verify/complete. If Reject → loop back to review_idea.

nodes.label: generate_roadmap
nodes.description: Creates a roadmap artifact for structured/complex work. Produces roadmap text (with optional markdown file write support). Backed by a strict internal prompt with mandatory output sections. Prepares planning output that eventually feeds into sync_tasks. Does NOT replace task syncing.

nodes.label: sync_tasks
nodes.description: Task ingestion and synchronization engine (formerly split_tasks). Creates/updates/overwrites/selectively merges tasks, maps and resolves dependencies, persists priority/category/metadata, keeps task graph valid and execution-order ready. Remains the sole DB-writing tool for tasks in both Fast and Structured flows.

nodes.label: review_idea
nodes.description: Critically reviews analysis results, evaluates solution completeness, and identifies optimization opportunities (formerly reflect_idea). The alias 'reflect_idea' is kept for backward compatibility.

nodes.label: process_thought
nodes.description: Structured thinking tool used at key checkpoints to improve output quality. NOT for every tiny step — checkpoint-based to avoid overhead. Required before: Fast/Structured flow selection, major user feedback rounds, generate_roadmap, sync_tasks, when blocked/conflicted, and before final verification for complex tasks. Records a step in the reasoning chain with fields: thought, thought_number, total_thoughts, next_thought_needed, stage, focus.

nodes.label: AgentFlow Redesign Plan v2
nodes.description: Full server-side redesign of MCP tool surface, task lifecycle, evidence model, and external LLM provider integration. Dated 2026-05-24. Targets 10 MCP tools (12 during migration), honest task lifecycle with pass/fail/partial/needs_review verdicts, append-only task_findings table, pluggable external LLM providers via Vercel AI SDK, optimistic concurrency control, and manual mode fallback.

nodes.label: Discriminated Union Pattern (z.discriminatedUnion)
nodes.description: Use of Zod's z.discriminatedUnion('action', [...]) instead of z.object({action: enum}).superRefine(...) for polymorphic tools. Discriminated unions export to JSON Schema as oneOf with each branch carrying its own correct required array. This is a load-bearing fix because superRefine rules are invisible to zod-to-json-schema, causing the MCP client to see all fields as optional.

nodes.label: External LLM Provider Layer
nodes.description: Pluggable LLM provider integration using Vercel AI SDK (ai package). Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, and DeepSeek via env-configurable providers. Includes model discovery (per-provider model-list fetchers with TTL cache), selection strategies (latest_code, latest_reasoning, cheapest, fastest, manual), and a no-LLM manual mode fallback. Provider swap requires only one env var change.

nodes.label: 10-Tool MCP Surface
nodes.description: Target of 10 MCP tools post-deprecation (12 during migration). Organized by capability: project_view, project_edit, project_delete, task_view, task_edit, task_delete, task_lifecycle, context_get, workflow_run, artifact_record. Each polymorphic tool uses discriminatedUnion on 'action' or other discriminator. Destructive operations are in separate tools with confirm + dry_run + reason + audit requirements.

nodes.label: Task Lifecycle with Verdicts
nodes.description: Replacement for execute_task → verify_task → complete_task with a single task_lifecycle tool supporting pass/fail/partial/needs_review verdicts. fail and partial become first-class outcomes with required failureReason and nextStrategy fields. finalize action requires expectedVersion for optimistic locking. Nested discriminated union on verdict so per-verdict required fields are visible in JSON Schema.

nodes.label: task_findings Table
nodes.description: Append-only evidence trail table per task. Stores attempts, blockers, decisions, failures, partial results, successes, and thoughts. Has denormalized project_id (resolved from task_id at write time) for fast project-level queries. Never exposed for UPDATE/DELETE at the API layer — only appends. Indexed on (task_id, created_at DESC), (project_id, created_at DESC), (task_id, kind), (project_id, kind, type).

nodes.label: Optimistic Concurrency Control
nodes.description: Version-based conflict detection on tasks. Every task has a version integer (default 1). Single-task writes pass expectedVersion — mismatch returns CONFLICT with current task body. Multi-task writes (reorder, merge) pass expectedVersions map — all validated atomically in a transaction; any mismatch aborts the entire batch. finalize (most committal action) also requires expectedVersion. Other lifecycle actions bump version but don't require expectedVersion.

nodes.label: Manual Mode (WORKFLOW_MODE=manual)
nodes.description: When WORKFLOW_MODE=manual or LLM_PROVIDER=none, workflow_run does not call any LLM. Instead it returns a structured payload (mode, workflow, purpose, inputRequired, steps, outputSchema, qualityChecklist, nextRecommendedCalls) that turns the main coding agent into the reasoning engine while the MCP server provides structure. Keeps the server useful as a pure task tracker with zero API keys.

nodes.label: Project Identity Strategy
nodes.description: Dual identifiers for projects: git_remote_url (Primary, Strong Identity — UNIQUE) and local_path (Secondary, Weak Identity / Fallback — not unique). Git URL normalization: strip whitespace, remove trailing .git. Two folders with the same normalized Git URL share the same Project ID. Agent is responsible for resolving project_id; server enforces the requirement with Smart Rejection Logic that either provides the matching ID or instructs the agent to call list_projects/create_project.

nodes.label: Template System
nodes.description: AgentFlow builds replies from internal markdown templates in src/prompts/templates_en/ by default. If TEMPLATES_USE is set, it first checks src/prompts/templates_<TEMPLATES_USE>/. Falls back to templates_en if a template is missing. Final prompt text can be overridden by env vars: MCP_PROMPT_<PROMPT_KEY> (full replace) or MCP_PROMPT_<PROMPT_KEY>_APPEND (append). Template caching eliminates disk I/O on repeated tool calls (~95% faster on warm loads).

nodes.label: Task Archiving
nodes.description: Automatically archives completed tasks older than ARCHIVE_AFTER_DAYS (default 30) to prevent tasks.json from growing indefinitely. Archive structure: data/archive/YYYY-MM.json. Archives are searchable via query_task (searches current + archived). Also backs up tasks to data/memory/ on clear_all_tasks.

nodes.label: MiniSearch Integration
nodes.description: Replaces shell-based search (grep/findstr) with MiniSearch library for fuzzy matching, cross-platform consistency, and no shell spawning overhead. Search index built on startup from all active tasks, updated on writes. Fields indexed: name, description, notes, implementationGuide, summary. Config: fuzzy 0.2, prefix matching, boost on name (2x) and description (1.5x).

nodes.label: Write Batching
nodes.description: Debounces file writes to reduce I/O: 100ms debounce window. Instead of writing immediately, writes are scheduled; if another write comes within 100ms, the previous is cancelled. After 100ms of no writes, the file is finally written. 10 task creates → 1 file write instead of 10.

nodes.label: Template Caching
nodes.description: In-memory cache for template content in src/prompts/loader.ts using a Map<string, string>. Cache key: {TEMPLATES_USE}:{templatePath}. Cold load ~0.24ms, warm load ~0.01ms (95% faster).

nodes.label: SQLite Migration
nodes.description: Migration from JSON file system to SQLite database for ACID compliance, crash safety, and complex queries. Orders of magnitude faster than JSON: estimated 15ms vs >500ms for 100 writes. Uses better-sqlite3 with optional Supabase adapter.

nodes.label: Core Pain Points
nodes.description: Three core pain points the system addresses: (1) Memory Loss — AI assistants lack task memory across conversations; solved by Task Memory Function. (2) Structure Chaos — complex tasks lack systematic management; solved by Structured Task Decomposition. (3) Repetitive Work — inability to utilize past experiences; solved by Knowledge Accumulation and Experience Reference.

nodes.label: Workflow Lifecycle
nodes.description: Core workflow: Plan → Execute → Verify → Complete. Phase 1 (Context): process_thought + init_project_rules. Phase 2 (Planning): plan_task → analyze_task → reflect_task → split_tasks. Phase 3 (Execution Loop): list_tasks → execute_task → (agent acts) → update_task_content → verify_task → complete_task. The server is passive — no auto-chaining. The agent is the orchestrator.

nodes.label: Idea Phase vs Task Phase
nodes.description: Separation of Concerns architecture: Idea Phase (workflow_steps table) handles pure reasoning, brainstorming, planning — safe space for 'messy' thoughts. Task Phase (tasks table) handles concrete execution and tracking — strict state management. The Bridge: split_tasks acts as a One-Way Bridge consuming an Idea (Reflection) and producing Tasks. Mandatory sequence: plan_idea → analyze_idea → reflect_idea (no skipping).

nodes.label: Prompt Customization
nodes.description: Users can customize system prompts via environment variables without modifying code. Two modes: Override (MCP_PROMPT_<FUNCTION_NAME> — full replacement) and Append (MCP_PROMPT_<FUNCTION_NAME>_APPEND — adds to existing). Supports dynamic parameter placeholders like {description}, {summary}, {task}, etc. Configuration via .env file or directly in mcp.json. Also supports custom template folders via TEMPLATES_USE.

nodes.label: Task Complexity Assessment
nodes.description: Evaluates task complexity based on multi-dimensional criteria: description length, technical term count, dependency count, file operations count. Produces weighted complexity score with levels: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, VERY_HIGH. Generates handling recommendations. Implemented in assessTaskComplexity function.

nodes.label: Conversation History Module
nodes.description: Capture and manage conversations between user and system when ENABLE_DETAILED_MODE=true. Records all tool requests and responses, associates messages with specific tasks via conversationHistory field. Provides API endpoint /api/tasks/:taskId/conversation and displays history in web UI. Stores timestamps and tool names with each message.

nodes.label: Template Quality Audit
nodes.description: 69 templates across 16 directories rated: executeTask/index.md (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐), verifyTask/index.md (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐), planTask/index.md (⭐⭐⭐⭐), analyzeTask/index.md (⭐⭐⭐⭐), processThought.md (⭐⭐⭐⭐), queryTask.md (⭐⭐ — needed examples), clearAllTasks.md (⭐ — needed warning). All fixed: focus-specific reflection guidance added, final quality checklist added, usage examples added, data loss warning added.

nodes.label: Smart Tool Suggestions
nodes.description: Templates include '💡 Smart Tool Suggestions' sections guiding agents to use other MCP tools with fallbacks: Perplexity for research, Clear Thoughts for decisions, Context7 for docs. Example format includes Primary recommendation and Fallback with a note that tools are optional.

nodes.label: Vibe Coder Features
nodes.description: Vibe-friendly features for UI/UX development: Focus Modes (6 including 'vibe'), Design Tokens in process_thought, Emoji Indicators, Task Categories (frontend, design), Exploration Stage. Missing features: Screenshot Attachment (🔴 High), Figma Integration (🔴 High), Color Palette Preview (🟡 Medium), Component Status Board (🟡 Medium).

nodes.label: Schema Organization
nodes.description: Extracted all Zod schemas from taskTools.ts into src/tools/task/schemas.ts (~290 lines), organized by category: Planning (planTaskSchema, analyzeTaskSchema, reflectTaskSchema), Management (syncTasksSchema, listTasksSchema, queryTaskSchema, getTaskDetailSchema), Execution (executeTaskSchema, verifyTaskSchema, completeTaskSchema), CRUD (deleteTaskSchema, clearAllTasksSchema, updateTaskContentSchema). Functions remain in taskTools.ts; full extraction deferred to minimize risk.

nodes.label: Template Stage Map
nodes.description: Exact mapping of pipeline stages to markdown template files. Thinking: processThought/index.md + moreThought.md or completedThought.md. Planning (plan): planIdea/index.md + hasThought.md or noThought.md. Analyze: planIdea/analyze.md + optional analyzeIteration.md. Review: planIdea/review.md. Roadmap: generateRoadmap/index.md. Task sync: syncTasks/index.md + optional taskDetails.md. Execute: executeTask/index.md + conditional sub-templates. Verify: verifyTask/index.md. Complete: completeTask/index.md.

nodes.label: verify_task Fake Gate
nodes.description: verify_task unconditionally writes verificationStatus='passed' regardless of whether the agent actually verified anything. complete_task then guards on that flag, making verify→complete a tautological two-step that adds zero value. This is a blocking issue for honest task tracking. The v2 redesign replaces verify_task + complete_task with a single task_lifecycle tool supporting pass/fail/partial verdicts.

nodes.label: No Failure Flow
nodes.description: Current system has no failure flow — a failed task cannot be recorded as failed. The only outcomes available are 'in progress' or 'completed'. Agents have nowhere to write 'tried X, failed because Y, next try Z'. The v2 redesign introduces fail and partial verdicts with required failureReason and nextStrategy fields.

nodes.label: client_active_project
nodes.description: New table mapping client_id (PK, FK to clients) to project_id (FK to projects). Backs client-scoped project_edit(action=set_active). Each MCP client has its own active project — no global state to collide on. Prevents one agent from silently changing another's context.

nodes.label: lesson_summaries
nodes.description: New table for LLM-generated lesson summaries: id, project_id (FK), topic, summary, source_finding_ids (JSON array), created_at, generated_by_model. Populated by workflow_run(workflow=summarize_lessons). Keeps context_get(type=lessons) cheap and token-bounded.

nodes.label: llm_settings
nodes.description: Single-row table (CHECK id=1) storing LLM configuration: provider, model, selection_strategy, workflow_mode, base_url, max_tokens, temperature, refresh_ttl_hours. Backs GUI Settings → LLM panel. API keys are NOT stored here — remain env-only for security. Env vars are fallback when no row exists or LLM_CONFIG_LOCK=true.

nodes.label: Migration Phases (v2 Redesign)
nodes.description: Phase 1 (Schema Reshape — no LLM): 12 tools, task_findings table, task_lifecycle with real verdicts, artifact_record, context_get, optimistic concurrency, manual mode. Phase 2 (LLM Provider Layer): Vercel AI SDK, model discovery, GUI settings panel. Phase 3 (Optional): MCP Prompts and Resources, reduced tool list to ~7-9. Phase 4: Shim removal, surface drops to 10 tools.

nodes.label: System Limitations
nodes.description: Current limitations: file storage not suitable for multi-user concurrency, lacks user authentication and permission control, summary generation uses simple rules, file processing does not read actual file content (only generates summary information). Future improvements: migrate to database storage (done — SQLite), add user management, advanced summary algorithms, task priority and time planning, progress tracking, enhanced file association.

nodes.label: Agent Passive Design
nodes.description: The MCP server tools are passive: no auto-chaining. Calling plan_task does NOT automatically call split_tasks. Calling execute_task does NOT automatically write code. The agent is the orchestrator — it examines output and decides the next tool. This design keeps the agent in control, allowing iteration on a plan 5 times before committing, or failing verification and going back without the system forcing forward.

nodes.label: Hard Test Suite Results (SQLite)
nodes.description: 5 scenarios tested: Complex Workflow (✅ PASS — API task correctly blocked until DB task completed), Integrity Constraints (✅ PASS — cannot delete completed tasks), Batch Performance (✅ PASS — 14.18ms for 100 tasks, ~0.14ms per task), Search Performance (✅ PASS — 2.87ms hybrid MiniSearch+DB), Complexity Logic (✅ PASS — correctly identified High Complexity). Default search page size is 5.

nodes.label: Comprehensive Workflow Test
nodes.description: 5 test cases from logs/test_output.txt: Case 1 (Happy Path) ✅ PASS, Case 2 (Cross-Project Isolation) ✅ PASS — new step correctly routed to Project A based on inputStepId, Case 3 (Invalid Input ID) ✅ PASS, Case 4 (Broken Chain: Plan → Reflect) ✅ PASS, Case 5 (Split Tasks with Invalid Context) ✅ PASS — graceful degradation.

nodes.label: clearAllTasks Templates
nodes.description: Template files for clearAllTasks tool: index.md (base template with {responseTitle}, {message}, {backupInfo} placeholders), cancel.md (operation not confirmed message with ⚠️ irreversible warning), empty.md (no tasks to clear message), backupInfo.md (backup file notification with {{backupFile}} placeholder).

nodes.label: destructive_audits
nodes.description: Audit log table for destructive operations (project_delete and task_delete in execute mode). Records caller, reason, affected IDs, and timestamp. NOT foreign-keyed — rows outlive the projects/tasks they describe (survive CASCADE deletes).

nodes.label: Workflow Definitions
nodes.description: Static TS definitions for all 11 workflow_run workflows: plan, analyze, review, split_plan, process_thought, record_decision, review_task_quality, build_context_pack, summarize_lessons, detect_duplicates, generate_release_summary. Each definition includes purpose, inputRequired, steps, outputSchema (Zod), qualityChecklist, nextRecommendedCalls. Used both for manual-mode responses and as single source of truth for LLM agent-mode output schemas.

nodes.label: safeParseTool
nodes.description: Wrapper in src/utils/schemaParse.ts that produces MCP-compatible errors with discriminator hints. When a discriminated union's discriminator is missing, the error includes valid action values. Routes through toToolErrorResponse so CONFLICT bodies also surface inline.

nodes.label: Golden Fixture Schema Test
nodes.description: Scripts/export-tool-schemas.mjs writes every tool's JSON Schema to tests/fixtures/schemas/*.json. Supports --check mode for CI to assert generated schemas match fixtures. Normalizes discriminated anyOf → oneOf. audit-superrefine.mjs fails CI if any new tool uses superRefine for conditional required fields.
